blocks.h2: What a Fireplace Service Visit Includes
blocks.body: Before the first cold night, we clean the burner and pilot assembly, check the thermocouple or thermopile, inspect the logs and their position, test the ignition and remote and leak-test every gas fitting. For direct-vent units, we check the glass seal and the vent cap outside. It's a short visit that prevents the most common winter service calls.

blocks.h2: What Affects the Price of Fireplace Service
blocks.body: A cleaning and safety check is the simplest visit. Replacing a thermocouple, igniter or valve costs more because of the part. Running a new gas line for a conversion depends on the distance from the existing pipe and the route. We diagnose first, then give you a flat price for what your fireplace actually needs.

blocks.h2: Gas Fireplace Questions From Elmhurst Homeowners

items.q: Can my wood fireplace be converted to gas?
items.preview: Often, if the chimney is sound.
items.answer: Often. We run the gas line and install the valve. A chimney specialist handles any flue work.

items.q: Why won't my pilot stay lit?
items.preview: A dirty pilot or weak thermocouple.
items.answer: Usually a dirty pilot or a weak thermocouple or thermopile.

items.q: Does the damper need to stay open with gas logs?
items.answer: Yes. Vented logs need the damper held partly open.
Early fall, before the first cold night.

items.q: Why does my fireplace remote not work?
items.answer: Often dead batteries in the remote or the receiver. If not, the valve or wiring may need service.

items.q: Is it normal for a gas fireplace to smell the first time each fall?
items.answer: A brief dusty smell is common as dust burns off. A gas smell is not. If you smell gas, leave and call Nicor Gas.

items.q: How much does gas fireplace repair cost in Elmhurst?
items.preview: It depends on the part. You'll approve a flat price first.
items.answer: It depends on what failed and the type of fireplace. You'll approve a flat-rate price before we start.
